about: Falsifiable predictions for Flint (RecursiveSI/flint, 39.8B total / ~2.5B active MoE) on odie, written by Recipe Maker BEFORE any replay of lane flint-1030 returned numbers (the two servers had been up ~3 min; no replay result existed). Do not edit the predicted numbers after the measurements land; add a measured block beside them.
recipe: recipes/odie-flint-q4km-1perCard.json (every input tagged; ASSUMPTION marks each that rests on no Flint or llama.cpp-SYCL measurement)
model: src/model.js residentTerms + residentAgentPlan: decode t = engine_slowdown x (bytes x a + layers x c x batch mult) + KV(depth) x a / kv_read_eff, with a and c fitted on two measured llama.cpp-SYCL B70 decode anchors; prefill per read = chunks x (file bytes x a) + T x (slowdown x linear + attn x depth); agents split over the two instances by conversation affinity, each share replayed by agentTurnPredict (the per-turn model of the rescores) with Dn at min(agents on the card, slots)
binding_note: n=1: the agent alone cycles (binding agents); its turn is 64 % decode, 24 % prefill, 12 % tool gap, so decode dominates. n=4 and n=8: each card is decode-bound at its two slots (server busy 100 %); at n=8 two conversations per card wait for a slot
leverage: one-at-a-time sensitivity on turns/agent-min at n=4 (base 3.75): prefix re-read 300 / 6,000 tokens a turn -> 4.60 / 2.20; attention at depth 4e-6 / 1.6e-5 ms -> 4.50 / 2.75 (P 1,682 / 643); kv_read_eff 1.0 / 0.3 -> 4.20 / 3.20; answer length 0.5x recorded -> 5.50 turns but 17.8 useful tok/s. A llama-server that misses its SWA context checkpoint re-reads the whole ~80k prompt each turn: 0.3 turns/agent-min at n=4 (not the base case)
gaps: no slot queue in agentReplaySim: at n=8 four conversations share a card with two slots; modelled as processor sharing at the two-slot decode rate (work-conserving, so turns/s holds; per-turn latency spread does not), with no slot-restore cost from --cache-ram
each instance replays recorded agents 0..k-1 (both cards replay the same agents), not the proxy's actual assignment
answer length: no Flint replay, so the recording's own lengths (out_vs_recorded 1.0); Flash-Next wrote 0.4x, Ornith 0.7x
tokenizer: Flint's own vocabulary assumed equal to qwen's token count
decode at depth has no SYCL depth anchor; prefill has no llama.cpp-SYCL resident-MoE anchor (both from vLLM XPU and the bandwidth fit)
falsifiers: turns/agent-min outside the all-low..all-high band at any agent count falsifies the resident model

why_it_missed: MEASURED: Flint ends a turn at about a quarter of the recorded length (out_vs_recorded 0.247 / 0.249 / 0.325) where the prediction used the recording's own lengths (1.0): useful tok/s falls with it, and turns rise because a turn is shorter
MEASURED: prefill at agent depth is about half the predicted 1,084 (server 564-600); README: build 12004 runs every Flint prefill on the TILE kernel because both XMX paths refuse attention sinks

MEASURED: the prefix re-read the prediction assumed (1,500 a turn) is not the server's: 182 of 184 n2 turns read only their growth; what re-read there is comes from agent 0's tool-list change in the trace (data/workload.json turn_model.servers.llamacpp-sycl-slots-swa)
MEASURED: at two agents a card decode halves (31.0 a request) instead of batching up to the predicted 86.5 a card
